2d7fa4788b.why: Each instruction establishes a distinct required register value or the final CF and ZF comparison results.

e8785087f7.why: Each vector needs a load, rounded multiply, addition, and store, followed by the required index update and SF result.

da9842714f.why: The shifts, word duplication, and separate broadcasts are needed to produce both preserved vectors from arbitrary initial xmm0 bits.

03aa1dba86.why: The independent rounded and low-word products require separate destructive computations before their sum, memory addition, store, and index update.

afa8101923.why: With arbitrary xmm6, the comparison masks, conditional negations, saturation, and widening cannot be simplified as ordinary zero-based absolute-value operations.

694d91af8d.why: Four independent SAD computations and four additions are required, and folding a load would require an equally costly copy of the preserved xmm5.

fb79e8a568.why: The four widened halves depend on arbitrary xmm0 bytes and each needs its own square-and-add computation before accumulation.

bb39a2f06f.why: Each of the five instructions produces a distinct required vector value, including the required clearing of its upper YMM half.

9cdbaee99d.why: SSE2 needs separate byte widening and word subtraction for each row, along with the four loads, two stores, and three required address updates.

b520db780a.why: Both vector additions already fold one source load, and the stores, index update, and flag-producing comparison are required.

34c9a93ea2.why: An SSE2 memory-source paddb would read sixteen bytes instead of the permitted eight, so the two qword loads, addition, store, and index update remain necessary.

91c93f7bc7.why: The byte load, memory-source addition, byte store, and index increment each produce a required effect.

35db6636c7.why: Arbitrary widening and coefficient registers prevent narrowing the word arithmetic, while the exact qword loads, saturated output, and pointer and flag updates remain necessary.
